doc.title: Yusef Lateef — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Flute, world instruments and first recordings
title: Taking up flute, and teacher John Cabera
summary: His response to the flute suggestion, and a Spanish teacher who steered Milt Jackson to vibraphone and wanted Lateef on oboe.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Now, uh getting back, back to uh your, your work with, pardon me, with Kenny Burrell.
Now, he suggested that, that your take up flute. What, what, what was uh, what was your response to that suggestion?

Well, the response was I just never thought of it, but I took him up on it, you know. I thought it might be interesting, and I’m glad I did. Uh...it’s interesting uh we had a teacher, his name was John Cabera, um he was from Spain, and uh I was in the class the day he suggested that Milt Jackson play the vibraphones.
We all wanted to play something.

And, of course, Milt became one of the world’s great vibraphonists. And he wanted me to play oboe at that time, and I said, “No” [chuckling], but years later I remembered that, and I started to play the oboe in the early ‘50s.

Um...and we played a lot of uh Spanish music, because his father was a musician and would send us compositions from Spain. I used to play the dances for the various high schools in Detroit, um...so I played with Kenny about a year and a half, but...from 1950 to about the middle of ’52.
